q: You keep a suspect 4 days without magistrate production. Wife wants immediate production. Which remedy fits?
expl: Illegal custody without 24-hr production invites habeas to produce body.
why: Habeas is speedy remedy for illegal detention. SI must produce within 24 hours.

q: Bonded child cannot afford court. Teacher sends postcard to top court. Why can court act?
options: Diluted standing for poor via letter
Only victim with lawyer can come
Letter needs fee to be valid
expl: For voiceless poor court treats letters as PIL petitions.
why: PIL dilutes locus for disadvantaged. Epistolary help reaches voiceless.

q: Who audits AP scheme money and reports for legislature scrutiny?
expl: Constitutional auditor audits and accounts committee examines.
why: CAG audits Centre and States. Removal is like top judge.

q: After 2015 striking of commission law, how are top judges picked?
options: Chief Justice with four seniors consulting
expl: Collegium survives; 2015 commission law struck for independence.
why: Collegium has CJI plus four seniors. Commission model did not survive.

q: Parliament wants to remove top judge for misconduct. Correct process?
expl: Removal needs proved cause with special majority both Houses.
why: Tenure safety guards independence. Ordinary service rules do not apply.
trapnote: Judge removal is not clerk discipline.

q: AP vs Union river dispute wants to start directly in Delhi top court. Allowed?
options: No must start in munsif court
expl: Federal Centre-State disputes start directly in top court.
why: Original jurisdiction avoids hierarchy for federal suits. It is not appeal.

q: President doubts new bill validity with no live dispute and wants view. Route?
expl: President can seek advisory opinion, respected but not decree.
why: Advice clarifies law without parties. It does not decide rights.

q: Tahsildar denies statutory compensation, no fundamental right involved. Wider help where?
options: Amaravati High Court for legal rights too
expl: High Court reaches other legal rights, wider than top court.
why: Top writs are FR-only heart-soul. High Court covers more legal wrongs.
trapnote: Never call top wider than HC.

q: Court registrar rejects tender unfairly. Can office be questioned for equality?
expl: Judiciary is State for admin acts, not judicial decisions.
why: Tender can face equality test. Judgment merits cannot be so challenged.

q: You seek 14-day custody with no reasons, magistrate grants mechanically. Remedy?
options: High Court can test remand legality
No court can look at remand
expl: BNSS keeps reasoned remand; habeas tests illegal custody.
why: Mechanical remand violates liberty. Writ court checks 24-hr rule.

q: Compare top writ guarantee vs High Court writ power. Correct?
options: Top FR-only; HC FR plus legal rights
Top all laws; HC only FR
expl: Top enforces FR only; High Courts reach wider legal rights.
why: Heart-soul means FR focus. High Court scope is broader.

q: Compare direct federal suit vs presidential reference. Distinction?
expl: Original suit binds parties; advice does not bind as decree.
why: One resolves dispute. Other clarifies doubt without lis.

q: Compare collegium vs struck 2015 commission model. True today?
expl: 2015 commission struck; collegium continues.
why: Court guarded independence. Collegium remains method.

q: Compare auditor removal vs clerk removal. Correct?
options: Auditor like top judge; clerk service rules
expl: Auditor has judge-like security; staff face discipline rules.
why: Audit needs tenure safety. Clerk follows conduct inquiry.

q: Compare stranger PIL for poor vs private suit for self. Difference?
options: Stranger allowed for voiceless; self needs own standing
Any passerby can file property suit
expl: PIL dilutes locus for poor; private needs aggrieved standing.
why: PIL is for unable victims. Private guards personal rights.

q: A.Top writs only for fundamental rights. B.HC writs for fundamental plus legal rights. C.Top must issue writ in every filing.
expl: A B on scope true; C false, always is absolute trap.
why: Scope split is FR-only vs wider. Must in every case is false.

q: A.Auditor 6yrs or 65 earlier. B.Reports seen by accounts committee. C.Minister can remove by order.
expl: Term and committee true; removal judge-like not minister will.
why: Tenure chain fixed. Half-truth hides in removal part.

q: A.Top court CJI plus 33. B.Amaravati is AP High Court seat. C.HCs cannot issue habeas.
expl: Strength 34 and Amaravati true; HCs have habeas.
why: Number and seat factual. Denying habeas is flat wrong.
trapnote: Denial of writ is red flag.

q: A.Undertrial cases gave PIL roots. B.Disclosure case expanded PIL. C.Letters treated for poor.
expl: Poor-prisoner roots, expansion case, letter practice all true.
why: History chain consistent. Each supports diluted standing.

q: A.Judge removal needs proved cause majority. B.Tender can face equality test. C.Judgment can be State bias claim.
expl: Removal and admin-State true; judgment not State action.
why: Admin side is State. Judicial decision is not.
trapnote: Do not extend State to judgments.
